EXPERIENCE
Lumen Travel | Frontend Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Sep 2025
- Rebuilt the hotel search results page in React with server-side rendering, cutting median load time from 3.8s to 1.6s and raising bookings per search 9% in an A/B test.
- Cut the booking flow's JavaScript from 410 KB to 260 KB by code-splitting the calendar and map widgets.
- Added keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels to the date picker, fixing all 14 accessibility issues flagged in the audit.
- Moving image resizing to the CDN, inlining critical CSS, preloading the two web fonts and deferring the analytics script, raised the checkout page's Lighthouse performance score from 52 to 91.
- Cut the landing page's largest contentful paint from 4.1s to 1.2s by adding loading="lazy" to the hero image.
- Documented the design-system tokens in Storybook so designers could check spacing and color values without asking engineers.
Westfield State University | Web Developer, IT Services | Metro City, USA | Apr 2024 - Aug 2024
- Cut the university sites' JavaScript bundle by 60% by converting their PNG images to WebP.
- Interviewed 8 department editors about publishing; the findings led to a preview mode that cut broken pages reported by students from 30 to 6 a month.
- Writes the accessibility checklist for all university web pages, reducing failed audits from 12 to 2 a semester.
- Rebuilt the course-catalog search with client-side filtering, cutting search time from 4 seconds to under 1.
PROJECTS
Transit Arrival Web App | Independent Project | TypeScript, React | Oct 2025 - Present
- Built a progressive web app showing live bus arrivals for 400 stops, used by about 900 riders a week.
- Cut cold-start time on slow 3G from 3.0s to 1.5s, a 75% improvement, by caching the stop list offline.
- Raised weekly returning riders by 10% in the first month, from 30% to 40%, by adding saved stops.
Library Room Booking | Hackathon, Team of 4 | Vue | Feb 2024 - Mar 2024
- Worked on the frontend of the booking flow using React and TypeScript.
- Wrote the booking calendar component and its tests, handling overlapping bookings and time-zone changes.
- Presented the demo to the library staff and handed over the code with setup notes.
SKILLS
Tools: TypeScript, React, Vue, Storybok, Angular
Methods: server-side rendering, accessibility, component testing

items.says: The timeline has an unexplained nine-month gap between the bachelor’s degree and the university web-development role.
items.because: No study or work is listed between June 2023 and April 2024, which may prompt questions.

items.says: The 9% booking result does not say whether it is a relative lift or a percentage-point increase.
items.because: A reader cannot interpret the A/B-test impact precisely.

items.says: The claim that keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels fixed all 14 accessibility issues is too broad.
items.because: An audit can identify other kinds of issues that those changes do not address.

items.says: The checkout performance result is buried after four implementation details.
items.because: A scanning reader may miss the measurable outcome until the end of the bullet.

items.says: Attributing the LCP improvement to lazy-loading the hero image is technically backwards in the ordinary case.
items.because: Lazy-loading a hero image commonly delays the largest contentful element and worsens or leaves LCP unchanged.

items.says: The Storybook bullet gives an unmeasured benefit and ends with filler wording.
Converting PNG images to WebP cannot ordinarily cut a JavaScript bundle by 60%, and the measured quantity is unclear.
items.because: WebP conversion reduces image-asset size, not JavaScript code, unless the images were embedded in the bundle.

items.says: The reduction in broken pages should open the bullet instead of following the interview details.
items.because: The result is more persuasive than the research setup and gives an immediate measure of impact.

items.says: “Writes” is the wrong tense for a role that ended in August 2024.
items.because: It makes the work sound current even though the position has ended.

items.says: The accessibility checklist’s practice or standard is unspecified.
items.because: The reader cannot see the accessibility practice behind the checklist, limiting the claim’s technical credibility.

items.says: The search-time result does not define what was timed.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether it covers server response, browser rendering, or the full user interaction.

items.says: “Under 1” omits its unit.
items.because: The endpoint is incomplete and cannot confidently be interpreted as a one-second result.

items.says: The audience measure in “900 riders a week” is undefined.
The 75% improvement is mathematically wrong.
items.because: A decrease from 3.0 seconds to 1.5 seconds is a 50% reduction.

items.says: Caching the stop list alone does not establish the stated total cold-start reduction.
items.because: Cold-start time includes other loading, execution, rendering, requests, and device performance.

items.says: The change from 30% to 40% is a 10-percentage-point increase, not a 10% increase.
items.because: A relative increase from the 30% baseline would be about 33.3%.

items.says: The bullet says React while the project heading says Vue.
items.because: The inconsistent framework descriptions make it unclear which technology the project used.

items.says: “Worked on the frontend” is vague duty framing without a specific contribution or outcome.
items.because: A recruiter cannot tell what was delivered or why it mattered.

items.says: The booking-calendar bullet gives deliverables and edge cases but no outcome or effectiveness measure.
items.because: The reader cannot see what the work enabled in the booking flow.

items.says: The demo and handover bullet does not state what the delivery achieved or provide a measure.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether staff accepted, ran, evaluated, or continued using the result.

items.says: The Tools list misspells Storybook as “Storybok.”
items.because: The typo is visible in the technical skills section and obscures a recognizable tool.

items.says: Angular is listed under Tools without supporting experience elsewhere in the résumé.
items.because: No entry shows Angular work, so a reader cannot assess whether it is a current, practiced skill.
